author: Nate Miller
title: Will Benson sent down to minors
desc: Will Benson was optioned to Triple-A after Monday's loss to the Brewers.
impact: With Elly De La Cruz (hamstring) set to rejoin the Reds on Tuesday, Benson was optioned down to the minors to make room in the roster. Benson has posted just a .643 OPS with three homers across 114 plate appearances in a part-time role for the Reds so far this year.

author: Nate Miller
title: Elly De La Cruz (hamstring) officially activated Tuesday
desc: Elly De La Cruz (hamstring) was activated off the IL ahead of Tuesday's game against the Brewers.
impact: De La Cruz ends up missing just over three weeks due to a hamstring injury, as he last played back on May 31. The two-time All-Star is in the midst of another strong season, posting an .855 OPS with 12 homers and 10 steals through 58 games. Will Benson has been optioned to Triple-A in a corresponding move.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Jake Bennett strikes out nine in no-decision
desc: Jake Bennett threw six scoreless innings Monday against the Rockies but did not factor into the decision. He allowed four hits, all singles, with no walks and nine strikeouts. Bennett generated 15 whiffs and gave up three hard-hit balls while working with a 2-0 lead before Boston's bullpen lost it in the ninth.
impact: Bennett delivered one of the strongest outings of his young career at Coors Field and is lined up to start at home against the Yankees on Saturday.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Aroldis Chapman blows save against Rockies
desc: Aroldis Chapman took the blown save and loss Monday against the Rockies after allowing three runs on four hits without recording an out. All four batters he faced reached on hits, including a Hunter Goodman single that was the only hard-hit ball Chapman allowed. His ERA rose from 0.83 to 2.08.
impact: Chapman has now taken losses in back-to-back outings after allowing one run against Toronto and three more against Colorado. Monday marked the first time he allowed four hits in an outing with Boston and the fifth time in 886 career appearances.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Ezequiel Duran crushes two-run homer
desc: Ezequiel Duran went deep Monday against the Marlins, launching a two-run home run in the fourth inning of Texas' 4-3 win. The homer, his sixth of the season, traveled 407 feet to center field off Tyler Phillips. Duran also made a key defensive play later in the game, throwing out Xavier Edwards at the plate as the potential go-ahead run.
impact: Duran has become a key contributor for Texas this season, with his multi-position eligibility adding value in deeper mixed leagues.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Jacob Latz records 14th save
desc: Jacob Latz tossed 1.1 scoreless innings Monday against the Marlins to earn his 14th save of the season. He entered in the eighth inning with the bases loaded and protected the lead by getting Jakob Marsee to ground out. Latz returned for the ninth and retired the side in order while needing 31 pitches to record the final four outs.
impact: Latz's 31-pitch outing could leave him unavailable for Tuesday's game after being used for a four-out save.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Kumar Rocker strikes out career-high nine in bulk relief outing
desc: Kumar Rocker allowed two runs on five hits over five innings Monday against the Marlins while recording a career-high nine strikeouts. Working behind opener Tyler Alexander, Rocker needed just 76 pitches to complete five frames and generated 20 swinging strikes with a 46 percent CSW. He also benefited from a key defensive play in the sixth inning when Ezequiel Duran cut down Xavier Edwards at the plate to end the frame.
impact: The outing was a strong bounce-back effort for Rocker after he was tagged for seven runs over 3.1 innings by the Twins in his previous appearance. He is scheduled to face the Blue Jays on Saturday to conclude a two-start week.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Brady Singer dominant in no-decision Monday versus Brewers
desc: Reds right-hander Brady Singer pitched seven scoreless innings with two hits and two walks allowed against seven strikeouts in a no-decision on Monday against the Brewers.
impact: Monday marked one of this season's toughest-luck no-decisions, as Singer was dominant in what would eventually be a 2-1 loss in extra innings. Singer threw 69 of his 106 pitches for strikes on the evening and certainly deserved a better fate. The right-hander sports a 4.81 ERA in 15 starts this season and is next lined up to take on the Pirates on the road on Sunday.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Will Vest nails down four-out save Monday versus Astros
desc: Tigers right-hander Will Vest pitched 1 1/3 scoreless innings to earn the save over the Astros on Monday.
impact: Vest was called upon with two on and two out in the bottom of the eighth and got a massive strikeout of Jasson Dominguez to end the threat. He then sat the Yankees down in order in the ninth, including a game-ending strikeout of Amed Rosario to seal it. Vest picked up his second save of the season, both of the multi-inning variety, as he sports a 5.61 ERA, albeit alongside a 3.60 xFIP and a 3.31 SIERA, across 26 outings on the season.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Framber Valdez excellent in win over Yankees Monday
desc: Tigers left-hander Framber Valdez allowed just one earned run with eight strikeouts in six innings while picking up the win over the Yankees on Monday.
impact: Valdez yielded four hits, and just one extra-base hit, with two walks against his eight strikeouts in silencing a suddenly scuffling Yankees offense in Monday's series opener. Monday marked the 10th time in 16 starts that Valdez has completed six innings, while he has nine quality starts, but just four wins on the season. He will take a 3.91 ERA into his next scheduled start, which is set for Saturday at home against his former team, the Houston Astros.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Riley Greene homers in win over Yankees Monday
desc: Tigers outfielder Riley Greene went 1-for-2 with a homer and two walks in a 5-3 win over the Yankees on Monday.
impact: Greene padded a 4-1 Tigers lead with a fifth-inning solo homer to right field off of Yankees ace Gerrit Cole. The long ball was Greene's ninth of the season as he continues to put together an All-Star type of season. The 25-year-old is slashing .292/.385/.445 with nine homers, 40 runs, 34 RBI, and one stolen base across 78 games this season.

author: Nate Miller
title: Austin Riley comes up with three hits Monday night
desc: Austin Riley went 3-for-4 with three singles in Monday's 1-0 loss to the Padres.
impact: Riley was the only Braves hitter that bothered to bring his bat to the ball game Monday night. The two-time All-Star picked up three of his club's seven hits, including a ninth-inning single off Padres closer Mason Miller that made things at least a little interesting. Riley has finally been showing some life at the plate again lately, going 9-for-23 while hitting safely in 5-of-6 games.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Louis Varland nails down save Monday versus Astros
desc: Blue Jays right-hander Louis Varland pitched a scoreless ninth inning to pick up a save in a 4-2 win over the Astros on Monday.
impact: Varland got the ball with a two-run lead in the ninth, but immediately brought the tying run to the plate after issuing a leadoff walk to Yainer Diaz. However, Varland would set the Astros down in order from there, striking out pinch-hitter Taylor Trammell to end it. Varland is now a clean 16-for-16 in save opportunities and sports a 0.84 ERA and a 0.93 WHIP with 58 strikeouts against 12 walks through 38 appearances and 43 innings this season.

author: Nate Miller
title: Grant Holmes effectively wild in Monday's outing
desc: Grant Holmes allowed one run on three hits and five walks while striking out four over 4 2/3 innings in Monday's 1-0 loss to the Padres.
impact: Holmes' spotty control continues to lead to early exits and limit his fantasy appeal. Granted, he couldn't help going just two innings in last week's rain-shortened start, but the righty has lasted five or fewer frames in 7-of-9 outings since the beginning of May. In that span, Holmes has turned in a 4.61 ERA, 1.59 WHIP, and 40-23 K/BB ratio across 41 innings.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Dylan Cease fans eight in no-decision versus Astros Monday
desc: Blue Jays right-hander Dylan Cease allowed two earned runs with four walks against eight strikeouts in a no-decision against the Astros on Monday.
impact: Blue Jays manager John Schneider elected to keep Cease in the game at over 100 pitches with two out in the sixth, but Jose Altuve notched a game-tying RBI single, taking away a potential win and a quality start from the right-hander. Cease nonetheless continued to provide plenty of fantasy value with eight more strikeouts, increasing his season-long total to 118, good for third-best in the big leagues and tops in the American League. The veteran will carry a 2.75 ERA into his next scheduled start at home on Saturday against the Rangers.
